parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a genuinely protective state layer — 2013 gender-identity public-accommodation and employment protections, a hate-crime penalty enhancement, no facility ban, and a July 2026 'low-risk' classification — with a hostile federal layer that reaches every visitor: visas and passports restricted to birth-sex markers, discrepancy-triggered case refusal contemplating fraud-based lifetime ineligibility, documented stranding, federal single-sex facility exclusion, and documented abuse in immigration custody (beatings, solitary, sexual abuse) plus conversion-therapy-style federal corrections policy if detained. Several orders are enjoined, but the passport regime was upheld in November 2025. State remedies work for street and service discrimination; they cannot offset federal border, facility or custody practice. Worst features are tier-1 universal document exposure and tier-2 custody abuse.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal Feb-2025 cable tags all trans cases, requires refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, and contemplates fraud-based lifetime ineligibility; visas issued M/F at birth only; travellers report passports blocked or confiscated and stranded abroad; at least eight foreign governments issued advisories by March-April 2025.
entry_documents.protection: Traveller keeps their home-country passport; existing X-marker documents remain valid to expiry; the fraud finding requires four elements, has limited waivers, and is never automatic; the civil-liberties suit remains pending.
entry_documents.interaction: State ease of marker change never touches federal visa issuance; the resulting mismatch then drives secondary screening and colours every later state-level encounter.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented immigration-custody abuse of trans detainees — forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, severe sexual abuse; from 2026 federal corrections adopted conversion-therapy-style policies (forced haircut, hormone removal, psychiatric drugging); security screening involves invasive pat-downs and outing risk.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute and a state penalty enhancement for identity-motivated violent crime since 2013; no state custody-placement restriction documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: An entry refusal or document discrepancy can move a visitor from the protective state into federal custody, where the hostile federal regime, not state rules, governs placement and care.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities nationwide, reaching federally funded buildings inside this state; elsewhere 21 state/provinces ban facilities and 4 criminalise in some circumstances, with one documented restroom arrest and men's-ward holding.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state has no facility ban per the equality map, and its 2013 act protects gender identity in public accommodations.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State permission is displaced at federally funded sites; the visitor has no override and no choice of venue when federal business or emergency care requires it.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders freeze funding, propose barring insurance reimbursement for trans under-18s, subpoena under-19 patient records nationwide, and describe youth gender-affirming care as mutilation; federal facility rules reach federally funded clinics.
care_services.protection: This state bans conversion therapy (2018), covers transition-related insurance (2016), and prohibits gender-identity discrimination since 2013; it is not among the 27 units banning youth care.
care_services.interaction: A minor traveller's care need could trigger both federal record-subpoena and funding regimes while state protections still bind the provider — outcome uncertain at federally funded sites.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy prioritises neutralising groups 'radically pro-transgender'; a DOJ reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; a 2025 poll found 66% support birth-sex document rules; official hostility is documented at the highest levels.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target people who merely disagree; this state created an LGBTQ+ commission (Jan 2025) and a July 2026 assessment groups it with units refraining from targeting trans adults.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal threat-framing raises the probability and severity of any stop or screening, while state institutions remain comparatively restrained.

minors_guardians.exposure: A federal order directs law enforcement to investigate and criminally prosecute those facilitating a trans minor's social transition; birth-sex marker rules apply equally to a trans minor's visa and passport; youth care is banned in 27 units.
minors_guardians.protection: This state bans conversion therapy for minors, protects gender identity since 2013, and has no youth-care ban; the school-prosecution order targets schools, not short-stay travellers.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans child travelling with a parent carries the same mismatched-document exposure at entry, and the parent's outing exposes the child to federal facility and screening rules.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific figures on anti-trans violence or enforcement of the 2013 penalty enhancement are documented; national bias-incident statistics persist; the state's own record is silent rather than reassuring.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime penalty enhancement since 2013, public-accommodation protection giving a remedy for service refusal, and a national hate-crime statute covering gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A documented service refusal or assault here has a realistic state remedy that exists in most peer jurisdictions — but its operation here is unverified.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Multiple federal measures are enjoined yet shifting, so exposure varies by travel date; the passport suit is unresolved; the 2023 panic-defence bill's disposition is unknown; gender-X licence status is stated only as of April 2020; the facilities map page returned 404.
remedies_unknowns.protection: A legal-aid FAQ tracks passport and document rules; a civil-liberties union sues for seven plaintiffs; state courts and the 2013 act function.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertainty concentrates at the federal border layer, where state remedies do not reach the traveller.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like Vesskar, exposure is routine and universal at identity checks, with documented detention/humiliation and only narrow, slow remedies. This case adds a written federal directive requiring refusal on document doubt and a possible lifetime bar, and documented custody abuse — heavier than Vesskar's discretionary verification — but offsets that with a state public-accommodation regime actually in force since 2013. Net: slightly above.

Kestrel Isles shows discretionary secondary screening ending in administrative refusal and return transport, with slow but existing appeals. Here screening is not discretionary but directive, with fraud-based ineligibility contemplated and documented abuse in federal custody after refusal. Remedies at the state level are stronger than Kestrel's appeal desk, but the custody tail is materially worse. Net: below 0.55-B.

Vellmaris has a national equality law that reliably releases and compensates despite one inconsistent officer. This state resembles that layer closely — protections, penalty enhancement, functioning courts. But the federal layer imposes a continuous document and facility exposure Vellmaris lacks, upheld by the supreme court, which state apology and compensation cannot remedy. Net: materially below 0.65-A.

Vellandra's register excludes transgender visitors categorically with no remedy. Here entry is not categorically barred to trans people as a class; refusal attaches to document discrepancy, waivers exist, litigation is live, and a whole state layer protects services and facilities. No register, no mandatory reporting, no eviction regime. Net: clearly above 0.35.

parsed.synthesis: Two regimes operate on one traveller. The state layer is genuinely protective and operative: gender-identity public-accommodation and employment protection since 2013, a hate-crime penalty enhancement, no facility ban, conversion-therapy ban, and a July 2026 assessment placing it among units that refrain from targeting trans adults — enough to keep street, lodging and restaurant exposure near the reduced-risk end. The federal layer is universal and enforced: birth-sex-only visa and passport markers, discrepancy-triggered refusal with a fraud/lifetime-ineligibility pathway, documented stranding, federal single-sex facility exclusion, and — only if entry fails or the traveller is detained — documented custody abuse and conversion-therapy-style corrections policy. Because the harshest operative rule governs the encounter, the border and custody exposures set the ceiling; state protections lift this well above jurisdictions whose own law restricts facilities or documents. Net: elevated risk, upper half — a good state inside a hostile federal machine.
